paper.title: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Task-Assignment with Uncertain Execution Times and Preferences

settings.name_in_paper: Heterogeneous multi-agent sequential task assignment with uncertain rewards, completion times and resource consumption
unmapped: Actions are N x M binary task-agent assignment matrices; each task to at most one agent
Stochastic task completion times in {C_l,...,C_u} block agent-task pairs (blocking bandits); learner knows C_l and C_u
Unknown stochastic per-agent resource consumption in [0,1] with expected per-agent budget constraints L_m; feasibility must be learned; violation penalty measured separately
Rewards from tasks assigned beyond resource capacity are not counted
Regret is alpha-approximate regret against OPT/(1+alpha), where OPT is the optimal policy value with known distributions; planner may use a (1+alpha)-approximate optimization oracle
settings.definition_quote: The goal of the planner is to maximize the total expected reward that the team receives over the problem horizon while ensuring that the resource consumption required for any assigned task is within the capability of the agent.

algorithms.name: Bandit Algorithm for Task Assigning (Algorithm 1), exact or (1+alpha)-approximate oracle

symbols.C_l: lower bound on task completion times
symbols.C_u: upper bound on task completion times
symbols.Lbar: maximum number of tasks the team can execute simultaneously
symbols.Delta_L_a: max_m Delta^L_{am}, violation gap of an infeasible assignment a (a left unspecified in the statement)
symbols.Delta_L_max: max over infeasible assignments a of total violation gap Delta^L_a

conditions: rewards, resource consumption in [0,1]; completion times in {C_l,...,C_u}

source.label: thm:inf_regret_stc_f
source.quote: If $T > MNBC_u$, the violation penalty $V_T$ defined in~\eqref{eq:violation_penalty} for Algorithm~\ref{alg:bandit} is bounded above by V_T \leq \mc O\Big( \frac{C^2_u}{C_l}\ln T + \frac{\bar{L}^2 \ln T}{(\max_{m}\Delta^L_{am})^2} + \bar{L} \max_{a\in \mc A^c}\Delta^L_{a} \Big)

results.notes: Bound on violation penalty V_T (expected constraint violation), not regret. The middle term's dependence on 'a' is ambiguous in the statement (the proof sums over infeasible a).

symbols.C_l: lower bound on task completion times
symbols.C_u: upper bound on task completion times
symbols.Lbar: maximum number of tasks the team can execute simultaneously
symbols.G_inf: sum over infeasible assignments a of 1/(max_m Delta^L_{am})^2

conditions: rewards, resource consumption in [0,1]; completion times in {C_l,...,C_u}

source.label: thm:sub_optimal_bound
source.quote: Given that $T > MNBC_u$ and Algorithm~\ref{alg:bandit} is an $(1+\alpha)$-approximate algorithm for some $\alpha \geq 0$, the regret $R^{\alpha}_T$ ... is bounded above by R^{\alpha}_T \leq \mc O\Big(\Big(\frac{1 }{\ul{\Delta}^\alpha } + C_u\Big)\frac{C_u}{C_l^2}NM\ol{L} \ln T +\sum_{a \in \mc A^c} \frac{\bar{L}^3\ln T}{C_l(\max_{m}\Delta^L_{am})^2} \Big).

results.notes: Regret is alpha-approximate regret R^alpha_T = OPT/(1+alpha) - E_T, OPT the optimal policy value with known distributions; alpha = 0 gives exact regret.

bound.expression_latex: \mc O\Big(\frac{1}{C_l} \sqrt{ C_u N M\ol{L} T\ln T} + \frac{C^2_u}{C_l^2}NM\ol{L} \ln T  +\sum_{a \in \mc A^c} \frac{\bar{L}^3\ln T}{C_l(\max_{m}\Delta^L_{am})^2}\Big)

symbols.C_l: lower bound on task completion times
symbols.C_u: upper bound on task completion times
symbols.Lbar: maximum number of tasks the team can execute simultaneously
symbols.G_inf: sum over infeasible assignments a of 1/(max_m Delta^L_{am})^2

source.label: thm:sub_optimal_bound
source.quote: Further, for any distribution of completion times and rewards, the regret is bounded as $R^{\alpha}_T = \mc O\Big(\frac{1}{C_l} \sqrt{ C_u N M\ol{L} T\ln T} + \frac{C^2_u}{C_l^2}NM\ol{L} \ln T  +\sum_{a \in \mc A^c} \frac{\bar{L}^3\ln T}{C_l(\max_{m}\Delta^L_{am})^2}\Big)$.

results.notes: Distribution-free over reward/completion time distributions, but still depends on violation gaps through G_inf.

symbols.C_l: lower bound on task completion times
symbols.C_u: upper bound on task completion times
symbols.Lbar: maximum number of tasks the team can execute simultaneously

source.label: thm:sub_optimal_bound
source.quote: Moreover, when Algorithm~\ref{alg:bandit} is an exact algorithm, for any $N,M,T, L$ such that $T = \Omega(C_u)$, there exists a problem instance for which the optimal regret of any task assignment algorithm is lower bounded by $R^{0}_T= \Omega(\frac{1}{C_l} \min \{\sqrt{C_u NM \ol{L} T}, \ol{L}T\})$.

results.notes: Proof obtained by reduction to Ito et al. (2024) Theorem 4.5; minimax construction.
